properties.name: Approving a node you authored no longer erases that you authored it — AUTHORED_BY's role becomes a set with a date per role, merged on write, migrated on open and import
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
THE CAUSE: an edge's identity in the store is (graph, type, from, to) — the role was a property, not part of the identity — so `authored_by(role=approver)` on a node the same contributor had authored REPLACED the author edge wholesale, `acted_at` included, and reported the edge it wrote. Every approver path went through it. flo2 caught it twice in one day from a compare_designs-built PR body; reflow2's own design had 389 approver-only edges it could no longer account for; dec:design-authorship-identity had promised the edge "is past tense and never changes".

THE FIX, at the cause: schema/core.yaml AUTHORED_BY carries `roles` (list:string) + `authored_at`/`reviewed_at`/`approved_at`. `DesignGraph::authored_by` merges into the set in canonical order; a role outside AUTHORED_ROLES is refused at the typed door. `normalize_authored_by_props` brings a legacy edge into shape and DROPS a legacy `role` found beside a set (an older binary's schema default, not a claim). `migrate_authored_by_roles` runs on every on-disk open, idempotent. `import_graph` normalises AUTHORED_BY edges on the way in. `authored_roles`/`edge_has_role` read both shapes. acknowledge_gap_by and acknowledge_defect_by route through `authored_by`. report.rs's two approver readers use `edge_has_role`. The MCP `role` enum is generated from AUTHORED_ROLES. check_intent_authority.py and smoke_mcp.py read the set.

THE CALL SURFACE IS UNCHANGED — `authored_by(role=…)`, `approver` on constructors and setters — so every skill, doc and tool description naming them stays true. The schema stamp did not move (no type names changed), so no upgrade doc is owed; the exported edge shape changed, so this is a MINOR bump.

FALSIFIED: reverting the merge to a replace fails exactly the three tests that assert merging (legacy author survives, both roles kept, order-independence). 11 tests in an_approval_does_not_erase_authorship.rs; one test (write approver twice, expect exactly [approver]) caught a real bug in the first draft — a legacy default applied to a fresh write — that two sibling tests had passed over (fact:lesson-a-legacy-default-applied-to-a-fresh-write…).

MEASURED on reflow2's own store at first open: 842 edges migrated, 0 legacy left. Core 160 binaries, MCP 71, clippy clean both crates and feature sets, smoke_mcp green, check_intent_authority 12 tests.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: recover the authors already displaced — that record is gone. The general asymmetry (edge writes preserve and report nothing) is recorded as dec:idea-should-an-edge-write-report-and-preserve-what-it-replaced-the-way-a-node-write-does.
